scenario.scenarioBackupFileName()\r\n\r\n    override fun createBackupFromScenario(scenario: CompleteScenario, screenSize: Point): ScenarioBackup =\r\n        ScenarioBackup(\r\n            scenario = scenario,\r\n            screenWidth = screenSize.x,\r\n            screenHeight = screenSize.y,\r\n            version = CLICK_DATABASE_VERSION,\r\n        )\r\n\r\n    override fun verifyExtractedBackup(backup: ScenarioBackup, screenSize: Point): CompleteScenario? {\r\n        Log.i(TAG, \"Verifying smart scenario ${backup.scenario.scenario.id}\")\r\n\r\n        backup.scenario.events.forEach { event ->\r\n            if (event.actions.isEmpty()) {\r\n                Log.w(TAG, \"Invalid scenario, action list is empty.\")\r\n                return null\r\n            }\r\n\r\n            if (event.conditions.isEmpty()) {\r\n                Log.w(TAG, \"Invalid scenario, condition list is empty.\")\r\n                return null\r\n            }\r\n\r\n            event.conditions.forEach { condition ->\r\n                if (condition.type == ConditionType.ON_IMAGE_DETECTED && (\r\n                            condition.path == null || !File(appDataDir, condition.path!!).exists())) {\r\n                    Log.w(TAG, \"Invalid screen condition, ${condition.path} file does not exist.\")\r\n                    return null\r\n                }\r\n            }\r\n        }\r\n\r\n        if (!screenCompatWarning) {\r\n            screenCompatWarning = screenSize != Point(backup.screenWidth, backup.screenHeight)\r\n        }\r\n\r\n        Log.i(TAG, \"Smart scenario is valid, has warnings: $screenCompatWarning\")\r\n        return backup.scenario\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    override fun reset() {\r\n        super.reset()\r\n        screenCompatWarning = false\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Tag for logs. */\r\nprivate const val TAG = \"SmartBackupEngine\""
```json
  }
}
```

```json
    "content": "# Data Structures & Backup Format\n\n## Overview\nThe application uses a ZIP archive format for backing up and sharing scenarios. This archive contains JSON files defining the scenarios and any associated image assets (for \"Smart\" scenarios).\n\n## Backup File Format (ZIP)\nThe backup file (`.zip`) structure is organized as follows:\n\n*   **Root Level:**\n    *   **Dumb Scenarios:** JSON files named matching `dumb-scenario-<ID>-.*\\.json`.\n    *   **Smart Scenarios:** JSON files named matching `smart-scenario-<ID>-.*\\.json`.\n    *   **Image Assets:** PNG files for image conditions, typically named with a timestamp or ID.\n\n### JSON Structure\n\n#### Smart Scenario (`ScenarioBackup`)\nRoot JSON object:\n```json\n{\n  \"version\": \"Integer (Database Version)\",\n  \"screenWidth\": \"Integer\",\n  \"screenHeight\": \"Integer\",\n  \"scenario\": {\n    \"scenario\": {\n      \"id\": { \"databaseId\": \"Long\", \"tempId\": \"Long?\" },\n      \"name\": \"String\",\n      \"detectionQuality\": \"Integer\",\n      \"randomize\": \"Boolean\",\n      \"keepScreenOn\": \"Boolean\",\n      \"eventCount\": \"Integer\",\n      \"stats\": { ... }\n    },\n    \"events\": [\n      {\n        \"event\": {\n            \"id\": { ... },\n            \"scenarioId\": { ... },\n            \"name\": \"String\",\n            \"priority\": \"Integer\",\n            \"type\": \"Enum (IMAGE_EVENT, TRIGGER_EVENT, etc.)\",\n            \"onEventAction\": \"Enum\"\n        },\n        \"conditions\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": { ... },\n                \"eventId\": { ... },\n                \"name\": \"String\",\n                \"type\": \"Enum (ON_IMAGE_DETECTED, etc.)\",\n                \"path\": \"String (Path to PNG inside ZIP)\",\n                \"area\": { \"left\": \"Int\", \"top\": \"Int\", \"right\": \"Int\", \"bottom\": \"Int\" },\n                \"threshold\": \"Int\",\n                \"minMatches\": \"Int\"\n            }\n        ],\n        \"actions\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": { ... },\n                \"eventId\": { ... },\n                \"name\": \"String\",\n                \"type\": \"Enum (CLICK, SWIPE, PAUSE, INTENT)\",\n                \"priority\": \"Int\",\n                ... (Action specific fields like x, y, duration)\n            }\n        ]\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### Dumb Scenario (`DumbScenarioBackup`)\nRoot JSON object:\n```json\n{\n  \"version\": \"Integer\",\n  \"screenWidth\": \"Integer\",\n  \"screenHeight\": \"Integer\",\n  \"dumbScenario\": {\n    \"scenario\": {\n        \"id\": { \"databaseId\": \"Long\", \"tempId\": \"Long?\" },\n        \"name\": \"String\",\n        \"repeatCount\": \"Int\",\n        \"isRepeatInfinite\": \"Boolean\",\n        \"maxDurationMin\": \"Int\",\n        \"isDurationInfinite\": \"Boolean\",\n        \"randomize\": \"Boolean\",\n        \"stats\": { ... }\n    },\n    \"dumbActions\": [\n        {\n            \"type\": \"String (DumbClick, DumbSwipe, DumbPause)\",\n            \"id\": { ... },\n            \"scenarioId\": { ... },\n            \"name\": \"String\",\n            \"priority\": \"Int\",\n            \"repeatCount\": \"Int\",\n            \"isRepeatInfinite\": \"Boolean\",\n            \"repeatDelayMs\": \"Long\",\n            \"position\": { \"x\": \"Int\", \"y\": \"Int\" },\n            \"pressDurationMs\": \"Long\"\n            ... (Swipe specific fields)\n        }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Database Identifiers\nThe application uses a custom `Identifier` class wrapping a `Long` database ID.\n*   `databaseId`: The persistent ID from the Room database.\n*   `tempId`: Used for unsaved objects (not relevant for backup files).\n",
```

```json
    "content": "# ADB Command Proposal\n\n## Objective\nEnable launching a specific scenario (Smart or Dumb) via an ADB command using its database ID.\n\n## Technical Implementation\n\n### 1. Android Manifest\nRegister a new Intent Filter in `AndroidManifest.xml` for `ScenarioActivity`.\n\n*   **Action:** `com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO`\n*   **Category:** `android.intent.category.DEFAULT`\n\n```xml\n<activity android:name=\".scenarios.ScenarioActivity\" ...>\n    <intent-filter>\n        <action android:name=\"com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO\" />\n        <category android:name=\"android.intent.category.DEFAULT\" />\n    </intent-filter>\n</activity>\n```\n\n### 2. ScenarioActivity Logic\nModify `ScenarioActivity.onCreate` and/or `onNewIntent` to handle the incoming intent.\n\n*   **Intent Extra:** `SCENARIO_ID` (Long) - The database ID of the scenario to launch.\n*   **Logic:**\n    1.  Check if the intent action matches `com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO`.\n    2.  Extract `SCENARIO_ID` from extras.\n    3.  Query the `ScenarioListViewModel` (or repository directly) to find the scenario by ID.\n        *   Check both Smart and Dumb repositories.\n    4.  If found, trigger the existing start logic (`startScenario(item)`).\n    5.  If the app needs permissions (Media Projection, Accessibility), the existing flow in `ScenarioActivity` should handle it naturally, provided we hook into `startScenario` correctly.\n\n### 3. ADB Command Example\n```bash\nadb shell am start -a com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO --el SCENARIO_ID <id>\n```\n*   `--el` denotes a Long extra.\n\n## Flow Diagram\n`ADB Command` -> `ScenarioActivity (onCreate/onNewIntent)` -> `Extract ID` -> `Find Scenario` -> `Trigger Permissions/Start Logic`\n"
  },

}
```

```json
    "content": "# React Scenario Previewer Specification\n\n## Objective\nCreate a standalone React web application (running locally on PC) to preview Smart AutoClicker scenario backup files (`.zip`).\n\n## Key Features\n\n### 1. File Import\n*   **Drag & Drop Zone:** Allow users to drag and drop a `.zip` backup file.\n*   **File Parsing:** Use a JS library (like `jszip`) to extract the contents of the uploaded file client-side.\n*   **Validation:** Check for the presence of valid JSON scenario files.\n\n### 2. Scenario List\n*   Display a list of all scenarios found in the backup.\n*   **Columns:** ID, Name, Type (Smart/Dumb), Event Count.\n*   **Search/Filter:** Filter by name or ID.\n*   **Selection:** Click a row to view details.\n\n### 3. Detailed Preview (Visualization)\n*   **Smart Scenarios:**\n    *   **Metadata:** Show global settings (Quality, Randomize, etc.).\n    *   **Events List:**\n        *   Display each Event with its Triggers (Conditions) and Actions.\n    *   **Image Conditions:**\n        *   Display the reference image (extracted from ZIP) for `ON_IMAGE_DETECTED` conditions.\n        *   Show detection area (coordinates) and threshold.\n    *   **Actions:**\n        *   List actions in execution order (Priority).\n        *   Show action details (Type, Coordinates, Duration, Intent params).\n*   **Dumb Scenarios:**\n    *   **Action Sequence:** Simple list of clicks/swipes/pauses in order.\n    *   **Looping:** Show repeat count/duration settings.\n\n### 4. Architecture (High Level)\n*   **Framework:** React (with TypeScript recommended).\n*   **State Management:** React Context or Zustand to hold the loaded backup data.\n*   **Styling:** Tailwind CSS or Material UI (MUI) for a clean, \"application-like\" look.\n*   **Libraries:**\n    *   `jszip`: For handling ZIP files.\n    *   `lucide-react` or `react-icons`: For UI icons.\n\n## Project Structure (Proposed)\n```\npchelper/\n├── public/\n├── src/\n│   ├── components/\n│   │   ├── FileUploader.tsx\n│   │   ├── ScenarioList.tsx\n│   │   ├── ScenarioDetail/\n│   │   │   ├── SmartScenarioView.tsx\n│   │   │   ├── DumbScenarioView.tsx\n│   │   │   └── ImagePreview.tsx\n│   ├── utils/\n│   │   ├── zipHandler.ts\n│   │   └── parsers.ts\n│   ├── App.tsx\n│   └── main.tsx\n├── package.json\n└── README.md\n```\n"
```

```json
    "content": "# Klick'r Project Blueprint\n\n## Introduction\nThis blueprint outlines the documentation and planned features for extending the Klick'r (Smart AutoClicker) application with ADB control capabilities and a companion PC preview tool.\n\n## Components\n\n### 1. Core Application Extensions\nWe are enhancing the Android application to support external automation control and better user identification of scenarios.\n\n*   **Scenario Identification:** We will modify the UI to explicitly show the Database ID for every scenario.\n    *   *Technical Detail:* [UI_CHANGES.md](UI_CHANGES.md)\n*   **ADB Control:** We will add a new Intent to allow starting specific scenarios via ADB commands using their ID.\n    *   *Technical Detail:* [ADB_COMMAND_PROPOSAL.md](ADB_COMMAND_PROPOSAL.md)\n\n### 2. PC Companion Tool\nA React-based web application to visualize scenario backups on a PC.\n\n*   **Location:** `pchelper/` directory.\n*   **Function:** Parses the application's backup ZIP files and provides a read-only preview of the logic, images, and settings.\n*   **Specification:** [REACT_PREVIEWER_SPEC.md](REACT_PREVIEWER_SPEC.md)\n\n### 3. Data Reference\nUnderstanding the backup format is crucial for the PC Companion Tool.\n\n*   **Format:** ZIP archive containing JSON models and PNG assets.\n*   **Structure:** [DATA_STRUCTURES.md](DATA_STRUCTURES.md)\n\n## Workflow\n1.  **User** creates scenarios in the Android App.\n2.  **App** displays IDs (`ID: Name`) for easy reference.\n3.  **User** exports backup (`.zip`).\n4.  **User** opens backup in **PC Companion Tool** to review/verify logic.\n5.  **User** uses **ADB** to trigger the verified scenario on the device programmatically:\n    `adb shell am start -a com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO --el SCENARIO_ID 123`\n",
```

```json
{
  "name": "write_file",
  "args": {
    "file_path": "pchelper/src/utils/zipHandler.ts",
    "content": "\nimport JSZip from 'jszip';\n\ninterface ScenarioFile {\n  id: string;\n  name: string;\n  type: 'dumb' | 'smart';\n  content: any; // Will be parsed JSON\n}\n\ninterface ImageData {\n  fileName: string;\n  dataUrl: string; // Base64 encoded image\n}\n\ninterface ParsedBackup {\n  scenarios: ScenarioFile[];\n  images: ImageData[];\n}\n\nexport async function parseBackupZip(file: File): Promise<ParsedBackup> {\n  const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(file);\n  const scenarios: ScenarioFile[] = [];\n  const images: ImageData[] = [];\n\n  for (const [relativePath, zipEntry] of Object.entries(zip.files)) {\n    if (zipEntry.dir) continue;\n\n    const fileName = zipEntry.name;\n\n    // Check for scenario JSON files\n    const smartScenarioMatch = fileName.match(/smart-scenario-(\\d+)-.*\\.json/);\n    const dumbScenarioMatch = fileName.match(/dumb-scenario-(\\d+)-.*\\.json/);\n\n    if (smartScenarioMatch) {\n      const id = smartScenarioMatch[1];\n      const content = JSON.parse(await zipEntry.async('text'));\n      scenarios.push({ id, name: content.scenario.scenario.name, type: 'smart', content });\n    } else if (dumbScenarioMatch) {\n      const id = dumbScenarioMatch[1];\n      const content = JSON.parse(await zipEntry.async('text'));\n      scenarios.push({ id, name: content.dumbScenario.scenario.name, type: 'dumb', content });\n    }\n    // Check for image files (PNG)\n    else if (fileName.endsWith('.png')) {\n      const dataUrl = await zipEntry.async('base64');\n      images.push({ fileName: fileName, dataUrl: `data:image/png;base64,${dataUrl}` });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return { scenarios, images };\n}\n"
  },
  "id": "write_file-1763938342667-d2c184461f257"
}
```

Please upload a .zip file.');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    try {\n      const parsedData = await parseBackupZip(file);\n      onFileParsed(parsedData);\n    } catch (err) {\n      console.error('Error parsing zip file:', err);\n      setError('Failed to parse the backup file. It might be corrupted or an unsupported format.');\n    }\n  }, [onFileParsed]);\n\n  const { getRootProps, getInputProps, isDragActive } = useDropzone({\n    onDrop,\n    accept: { 'application/zip': ['.zip'] },\n    multiple: false,\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <div\n      {...getRootProps()}\n      style={{\n        border: '2px dashed #cccccc',\n        borderRadius: '4px',\n        padding: '20px',\n        textAlign: 'center',\n        cursor: 'pointer',\n        backgroundColor: isDragActive ? '#f0f0f0' : '#ffffff',\n      }}\n    >\n      <input {...getInputProps()} />\n      {\n        isDragActive ?\n          <p>Drop the .zip file here ...</p> :\n          <p>Drag 'n' drop a Klick'r backup .zip file here, or click to select one</p>\n      }\n      {error && <p style={{ color: 'red' }}>{error}</p>}\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default FileUploader;\n"
```json
  },

}
```

All requested features have been implemented and documented.

**To verify the React application:**

1.  Navigate to the `pchelper` directory:
    ```bash
    cd pchelper
    ```
2.  Start the React development server:
    ```bash
    npm start
    ```
    This will open the application in your web browser, usually at `http://localhost:3000`.

You can now upload a Klick'r backup `.zip` file using the `FileUploader` to preview your scenarios.

**To verify the Android application changes (ADB command and UI ID display):**

1.  Build and install the `fDroid` debug version of the application onto an Android device or emulator:
    ```bash
    ./gradlew assembleFDroidDebug
    ./gradlew installFDroidDebug
    ```
2.  Launch a scenario by ID using ADB (replace `<scenario_id>` with an actual ID from your app):
    ```bash
    adb shell am start -n com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.fdroid.debug/com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.scenarios.ScenarioActivity -a com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO --el SCENARIO_ID <scenario_id>
    ```
3.  Open the Klick'r application on your device and navigate to the scenario list. You should see the scenario IDs prepended to the scenario names (e.g., `42: My Scenario Name`).

```json
{
  "id": "read_file-1763939243522-161f69a81b539",
  "name": "read_file",
  "response": {
    "output": "\nimport JSZip from 'jszip';\n\ninterface ScenarioFile {\n  id: string;\n  name: string;\n  type: 'dumb' | 'smart';\n  content: any; // Will be parsed JSON\n}\n\ninterface ImageData {\n  fileName: string;\n  dataUrl: string; // Base64 encoded image\n}\n\ninterface ParsedBackup {\n  scenarios: ScenarioFile[];\n  images: ImageData[];\n}\n\nexport async function parseBackupZip(file: File): Promise<ParsedBackup> {\n  const zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(file);\n  const scenarios: ScenarioFile[] = [];\n  const images: ImageData[] = [];\n\n  for (const [relativePath, zipEntry] of Object.entries(zip.files)) {\n    if (zipEntry.dir) continue;\n\n    const fileName = zipEntry.name;\n\n    // Check for scenario JSON files\n    const smartScenarioMatch = fileName.match(/smart-scenario-(\\d+)-.*\\.json/);\n    const dumbScenarioMatch = fileName.match(/dumb-scenario-(\\d+)-.*\\.json/);\n\n    if (smartScenarioMatch) {\n      const id = smartScenarioMatch[1];\n      const content = JSON.parse(await zipEntry.async('text'));\n      scenarios.push({ id, name: content.scenario.scenario.name, type: 'smart', content });\n    } else if (dumbScenarioMatch) {\n      const id = dumbScenarioMatch[1];\n      const content = JSON.parse(await zipEntry.async('text'));\n      scenarios.push({ id, name: content.dumbScenario.scenario.name, type: 'dumb', content });\n    }\n    // Check for image files (PNG)\n    else if (fileName.endsWith('.png')) {\n      const dataUrl = await zipEntry.async('base64');\n      images.push({ fileName: fileName, dataUrl: `data:image/png;base64,${dataUrl}` });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return { scenarios, images };\n}\n"
  }
}
```

'Yes' : 'No'}</p>\n      <p><strong>Total Events:</strong> {smartScenarioContent.events.length}</p>\n\n      <h4>Events:</h4>\n      {smartScenarioContent.events.length === 0 && <p>No events defined for this scenario.</p>}\n      {smartScenarioContent.events.map((event: any, eventIndex: number) => (\n        <div key={event.event.id.databaseId} style={{ border: '1px solid #eee', padding: '10px', margin: '10px 0' }}>\n          <h5>Event #{eventIndex + 1}: {event.event.name} (Type: {event.event.type})</h5>\n          <p><strong>Priority:</strong> {event.event.priority}</p>\n\n          <h6>Conditions ({event.conditions.length}):</h6>\n          {event.conditions.length === 0 && <p>No conditions for this event.</p>}\n          {event.conditions.map((condition: any, condIndex: number) => (\n            <div key={condition.id.databaseId} style={{ border: '1px dotted #ccc', padding: '8px', margin: '5px 0' }}>\n              <p><strong>Condition #{condIndex + 1}:</strong> {condition.name} (Type: {condition.type})</p>\n              {condition.type === 'ON_IMAGE_DETECTED' && condition.path && (\n                <div>\n                  <p><strong>Path:</strong> {condition.path}</p>\n                  <p><strong>Area:</strong> ({condition.area.left}, {condition.area.top}) - ({condition.area.right}, {condition.area.bottom})</p>\n                  <p><strong>Threshold:</strong> {condition.threshold}</p>\n                  <p><strong>Min Matches:</strong> {condition.minMatches}</p>\n                  {findImage(condition.path) ? (\n                    <ImagePreview dataUrl={findImage(condition.path)?.dataUrl || ''} alt={condition.path} width=\"150px\" height=\"150px\" />\n                  ) : (\n                    <p style={{ color: 'orange' }}>Image not found in backup: {condition.path}</p>\n                  )}\n                </div>\n              )}\n            </div>\n          ))}\n\n          <h6>Actions ({event.actions.length}):</h6>\n          {event.actions.length === 0 && <p>No actions for this event.</p>}\n          {event.actions.map((action: any, actionIndex: number) => (\n            <div key={action.id.databaseId} style={{ border: '1px dotted #ccc', padding: '8px', margin: '5px 0' }}>\n              <p><strong>Action #{actionIndex + 1}:</strong> {action.name} (Type: {action.type})</p>\n              {/* Display action-specific details based on action.type */}\n              {action.type === 'CLICK' && <p>Position: ({action.position.x}, {action.position.y}), Duration: {action.pressDurationMs}ms</p>}\n              {action.type === 'SWIPE' && <p>From: ({action.fromPosition.x}, {action.fromPosition.y}), To: ({action.toPosition.x}, {action.toPosition.y}), Duration: {action.swipeDurationMs}ms</p>}\n              {action.type === 'PAUSE' && <p>Duration: {action.pauseDurationMs}ms</p>}\n              {action.type === 'INTENT' && (\n                <div>\n                  <p>Package: {action.packageName}, Class: {action.className}</p>\n                  <p>Action: {action.action}, Data: {action.data}</p>\n                  <p>Flags: {action.flags}, Categories: {action.categories}</p>\n                  <p>Extras: {JSON.stringify(action.extras)}</p>\n                </div>\n              )}\n            </div>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      ))}\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default SmartScenarioView;\n"

Refers\r\n * to the [DumbActionEntity] documentation for values/type association.\r\n *\r\n * /!\\ DO NOT RENAME: ActionType enum name is used in the database.\r\n */\r\nenum class DumbActionType {\r\n    /** A single tap on the screen. */\r\n    CLICK,\r\n    /** A swipe on the screen. */\r\n    SWIPE,\r\n    /** A pause, waiting before the next action. */\r\n    PAUSE,\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Type converter to read/write the [DumbActionType] into the database. */\r\ninternal class DumbActionTypeStringConverter {\r\n    @TypeConverter\r\n    fun fromString(value: String): DumbActionType = DumbActionType.valueOf(value)\r\n    @TypeConverter\r\n    fun toString(action: DumbActionType): String = action.toString()\r\n}"

    ```bash
    adb shell am start -n com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.fdroid.debug/com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.scenarios.ScenarioActivity -a com.buzbuz.smartautoclicker.action.START_SCENARIO --el SCENARIO_ID <scenario_id>
    ```
3.  **Open the Klick'r application** on your device and navigate to the scenario list. You should see the scenario IDs prepended to the scenario names (e.g., `42: My Scenario Name`).

It seems like the React app is still having trouble accessing nested properties, indicating a mismatch between the expected and actual JSON structure of the parsed backup data. The error "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'databaseId')" suggests that an object expected to have a `databaseId` property (which is directly `id` in the backup JSON) is `undefined` at some point.

Based on the `DATA_STRUCTURES.md` and the Kotlin `ScenarioBackup` and `DumbScenarioBackup` definitions, the `scenario` object in `ScenarioFile.content` has an extra layer of nesting.

For `SmartScenarioView`:
*   `scenario.content` is `ScenarioBackup`.
*   `ScenarioBackup` has a field `scenario` (of type `CompleteScenario`).
*   `CompleteScenario` has a field `scenario` (of type `ScenarioEntity`).
*   So, `smartScenarioContent.scenario.name` should be `smartScenarioContent.scenario.scenario.name`.

For `DumbScenarioView`:
*   `scenario.content` is `DumbScenarioBackup`.
*   `DumbScenarioBackup` has a field `dumbScenario` (of type `DumbScenarioWithActions`).
*   `DumbScenarioWithActions` has a field `scenario` (of type `DumbScenarioEntity`).
*   So, `dumbScenarioContent.scenario.name` should be `dumbScenarioContent.dumbScenario.scenario.name`.

I will update both `SmartScenarioView.tsx` and `DumbScenarioView.tsx` to correctly access these nested properties.

✨ ## MODEL

The user is reporting that the "Image not found" message is displaying even though the images are present in the backup. This suggests the filename matching logic in `SmartScenarioView.tsx` is incorrect.

The `findImage` function currently does:
```typescript
const findImage = (path: string) => {
  const fileName = path.split('/').pop(); // Extract filename from path
  return images.find((img: ImageData) => img.fileName.endsWith(fileName || ''));
};
```

And the `parseBackupZip` function stores images like this:
```typescript
// Check for image files (PNG)
else if (fileName.endsWith('.png')) {
  const dataUrl = await zipEntry.async('base64');
  images.push({ fileName: fileName, dataUrl: `data:image/png;base64,${dataUrl}` });
}
```

The `condition.path` in the JSON usually looks like `scenarioId/Condition_number.png` or similar relative paths. The `fileName` in `images` array comes from `zipEntry.name`, which is the full path inside the zip (e.g., `123/Condition_2014036073.png`).

If `condition.path` is just `Condition_2014036073` (no extension) as suggested by the user's error message ("Image not found in backup: Condition_2014036073"), but the file in the zip is `.../Condition_2014036073.png`, then:
1.  We need to handle the missing extension in the match logic.
2.  We should probably match loosely on the filename, ignoring directory structure if possible, or try to construct the expected zip path.

Let's look at `ScenarioBackupFiles.kt` again.
```kotlin
internal const val CONDITION_BACKUP_MATCH_REGEX =
    """[0-9]+/$CONDITION_FILE_PREFIX-?[0-9]+$CONDITION_BACKUP_EXTENSION"""
// ...
private const val CONDITION_BACKUP_EXTENSION = ".png"
```
So normally it should have `.png`.

However, there is also:
```kotlin
internal const val LEGACY_CONDITION_BACKUP_MATCH_REGEX =
    """[0-9]+/$CONDITION_FILE_PREFIX-?[0-9]+"""
```
Legacy conditions might not have the extension in the backup file name? Or maybe the `path` stored in the JSON doesn't have it?

The user says: "Image not found in backup: Condition_2014036073". This implies `condition.path` is "Condition_2014036073".
The files in the zip are likely `123/Condition_2014036073.png`.

My `findImage` splits `condition.path` to get `Condition_2014036073`.
Then it checks if `img.fileName` (e.g., `123/Condition_2014036073.png`) ends with `Condition_2014036073`.
`"123/Condition_2014036073.png".endsWith("Condition_2014036073")` is **FALSE**. It ends with `.png`.

So I need to make the matching more robust. I should check if the image filename *includes* the condition path base name, or try appending `.png` to the condition path if it's missing.

Refined `findImage` logic:
1. Extract base filename from `condition.path` (e.g. `Condition_2014036073`).
2. Iterate through `images`.
3. For each image, extract its base filename (remove path and extension).
4. Compare base filenames.

Actually, safer approach:
Check if `img.fileName` ends with `path` OR `path + ".png"`.

If `path` is `Condition_2014036073`:
`img.fileName` (`123/Condition_2014036073.png`) ends with `Condition_2014036073.png`.

everything is looking better now we just need to fix the channels a ligth blue is showing up as a desert sand colour

✨ ## MODEL

The "light blue showing as desert sand" color issue confirms that the color channels are still incorrect.

"Light blue" is typically something like `(R=173, G=216, B=230)`.
"Desert sand" is yellowish/tan, maybe `(R=237, G=201, B=175)`.

If I swap Red and Blue:
Light Blue `(173, 216, 230)` -> `(230, 216, 173)` which is a yellowish/cream color (like desert sand!).

This means my **previous channel swap was incorrect or redundant**.

In `ImagePreview.tsx`, I implemented:
```typescript
                imageData.data[i] = bytes[i + 2];     // Red = Blue from buffer
                imageData.data[i + 1] = bytes[i + 1]; // Green = Green from buffer
                imageData.data[i + 2] = bytes[i];     // Blue = Red from buffer
                imageData.data[i + 3] = bytes[i + 3]; // Alpha = Alpha from buffer
```
This assumes the buffer was `[B, G, R, A]`.

If the result (Desert Sand) is `(230, 216, 173)`, and the original (Light Blue) was `(173, 216, 230)`, then I successfully created `R=230, G=216, B=173`.
This implies the *bytes in the buffer* at `i+2` was 230, and at `i` was 173.
So `bytes[i+2]` (Blue position in loop) was Light Blue's Blue component.
And `bytes[i]` (Red position in loop) was Light Blue's Red component.

If `bytes[i]` is 173 (Red) and `bytes[i+2]` is 230 (Blue), then the buffer order is **already** `[R, G, B, A]`.

The `scenario_viewer_v2.html` had this comment:
`// ARGB_8888 little-endian: buffer [B,G,R,A], swap B/R`

Maybe the HTML viewer was dealing with a specific export version, or I misinterpreted "Light Blue showing up as Desert Sand".

If "Light Blue" is the **correct** color, and it's **showing up** as "Desert Sand":
My renderer (Desert Sand) has `R=230, G=216, B=173`.
Correct (Light Blue) has `R=173, G=216, B=230`.

My renderer sets `R = bytes[i+2]` (230).
So `bytes[i+2]` is 230.
My renderer sets `B = bytes[i]` (173).
So `bytes[i]` is 173.

If the buffer has `bytes[i] = 173` (Red value) and `bytes[i+2] = 230` (Blue value), then the buffer is `[Red, Green, Blue, Alpha]`.

So, **no swapping is needed**. The raw data in the file is already RGBA.

I will revert the swapping logic in `ImagePreview.tsx` and just copy the bytes directly.

Wait, standard Android `Bitmap.copyPixelsToBuffer` copies `ARGB_8888` pixels. On Little Endian systems (most Android devices), `0xAARRGGBB` is stored in memory as `[BB, GG, RR, AA]`.
If the file was saved by dumping this buffer directly, it would be BGRA.

However, if the file was saved using `Bitmap.compress` (which makes PNG/JPEG), it's a standard file. But these are "raw" files.

If the app manually wrote bytes R, G, B, A, then it's RGBA.

Let's try reverting the swap. If `bytes[i]` is R, `bytes[i+1]` is G, `bytes[i+2]` is B, then standard `set()` works.

I will modify `ImagePreview.tsx` to remove the manual loop and use `imageData.data.set(bytes)` directly. This assumes RGBA.**Tool Command**:
